tasks.title: Daily-rotating install id and per-process session id

details.goal: An install identifier that is stable inside one UTC day and unlinkable across days, plus a fresh per-process session identifier, both from `node:crypto` random bytes and neither derived from the repository.
steps: Declare the interface and the three functions with the signatures above.

Implement the read/parse/compare path so a same-day file is reused.
Implement rotation: mint 16 random bytes as hex and write with flag `"wx"`, falling back to a read on `EEXIST`.
Implement `newSessionId` and make every filesystem error non-fatal.

tasks.title: Read SANGKAR_TELEMETRY in config and expose AppConfig.telemetry

details.goal: The consent switch is read in the one module allowed to read tool settings and travels as a value on `AppConfig`, so no other module ever reads the environment for it.
details.contract:
In `src/shared/config.ts` add:

export interface TelemetryConfig { readonly enabled: boolean; readonly dir: string }

and add `readonly telemetry: TelemetryConfig;` to `AppConfig`. `loadConfig` returns `{ enabled: env.SANGKAR_TELEMETRY !== "off", dir: join(dataDir, "telemetry") }`. tasks.title: Buffered recorder with a bounded flush and a never-throw sink

details.goal: One recorder owns the sink, the identity, the per-process `seq` and a bounded buffer, so a tool call only appends to an array and a broken or full disk can never fail a call.
steps: Declare `TelemetrySink`, `jsonlSink` and `nullSink` in `sink.ts` — one `appendFileSync` of the joined lines, `mkdirSync(recursive)` on first use, no clock and no date arithmetic.
Declare `FLUSH_AT_RECORDS`, `FLUSH_AT_MS`, `TelemetryOptions`, `Telemetry` and the two factories in `telemetry.ts`.
Implement `createTelemetry`: identity, context, the single session record, the stat-based bucket and the git-marker root kind.
Implement `recordCall`/`recordIndexRun` with the `seq` counter, the buffered line plus its UTC date, and `maybeFlush`.
Implement `flush` (group by date, one `sink.write` per group) and `close`, plus the `degraded` on-first-failure path with exactly one warn.
Implement `nullTelemetry`, then run typecheck and lint.

tasks.title: Telemetry unit suite: shapes, rotation, off switch, redaction, flush, stdout

details.goal: The module's contract is executable: exact record shapes, daily id rotation, the off switch, a throwing sink, the privacy invariant, the bounded flush and the absence of stdout writes.
details.contract:
Create `tests/telemetry.test.ts` using `bun:test` and `mkdtemp` under the OS temp dir, removed in `afterAll`. Import from `#shared/telemetry/record`, `#shared/telemetry/telemetry`, `#shared/telemetry/identity`, `#shared/telemetry/sink` (`nullSink`, `type TelemetrySink`) and `#shared/config`. Build envelopes with `#shared/envelope`'s constructors and hand-written specs; never call a tool handler and never touch a real database.

Required cases:
1. Shape per kind — `Object.keys(record)` equals the exact field list from plan.approach.md §3 for `call`, `index_run` and `session`, in that order (with `v` second), `v === 1` in all three, and the JSON round-trip is stable.
2. Daily install-id rotation — `resolveInstallId(dir, day1)` then `resolveInstallId(dir, day1 later hour)` returns the same `install_id` with `isFirstRun: false`; `resolveInstallId(dir, day2)` returns a different `install_id` with `isFirstRun: true` and leaves one file.
3. `SANGKAR_TELEMETRY=off` — `loadConfig({ env: { SANGKAR_TELEMETRY: "off" } }).telemetry.enabled === false`, while `env: {}`, `env: { SANGKAR_TELEMETRY: "" }` and `env: { SANGKAR_TELEMETRY: "OFF" }` all yield `true` (one spelling, case-sensitive), and `dir` is `<dataDir>/telemetry` in every case. The file-level off switch is deliberately **not** asserted here: `nullTelemetry()` takes no options and holds no path, so "it creates no `telemetry/` directory" could not fail — the real proof is TASK-010 Case B, which spawns the shipped CLI with `SANGKAR_TELEMETRY=off` and asserts the directory is absent after the child exits 0.
4. Throwing sink — a `TelemetrySink` whose `write` throws does not reject: `recordCall` returns, `flush`/`close` return, and exactly one `warn` was logged. Assert nothing about the caller's envelope: a `void` method over a copied whitelist cannot mutate a frozen input, so such a case is a tautology.
5. Redaction invariant — build a `CallSpec` whose `suppliedNames` are `["query", "file"]` and whose `args` and payload contain `handleRequest` and `/home/x/secret-repo/src/core.ts`; take `JSON.stringify(callRecordOf(...))`, **parse the line**, and deep-walk every value except the `arg_names_set` array itself, asserting no value contains `handleRequest`, `/home/x/secret-repo`, `secret-repo` or `core.ts`; assert `arg_names_set` is exactly `["file", "query"]`. A substring check on the whole line cannot express this, because those names are supposed to be present.
6. `stale_reason` is an enum — build a `call` record from an envelope whose `read_status.stale_reason` is the `trace` wording, `'"src/core.ts" was last written by generation 3'`, and assert the record's `stale_reason` is `"other"` and that no value of the parsed line contains `src/core.ts`, `core.ts` or `generation`; a second record built with `stale_reason: "root_mismatch"` keeps that value verbatim, and a third with no envelope records `null`.
7. Bounded flush — with 31 records appended and a fixed clock nothing is written; the 32nd writes one line per record in one append; separately, advancing the injected clock by 5 000 ms and recording once writes the buffer; `close()` always flushes, and a flush whose records straddle two UTC dates produces one file per date.
8. No stdout — scope the spy to the telemetry calls only: install the `process.stdout.write` mock immediately before the `recordCall`/`flush`/`close` calls of that one test and restore it immediately after. Never wrap the suite body, because bun's own reporter writes to stdout during the run and the spy would capture it.

Do not weaken a case to make it pass, and do not edit any other file.
steps: Create the file with a `tempDir()` helper (`mkdtemp` + `rm` in `afterAll`) and the envelope/spec builders.
Write the three shape cases against the exact field lists, including `v === 1`.
Write the rotation and off-switch cases with two injected dates and an injected `env`.
Write the throwing-sink case and the bounded-flush case with an injected `now`.
Write the two redaction cases: the deep-walked values with `arg_names_set` excluded, and the `stale_reason` enum.
Write the scoped stdout-spy case, run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/telemetry.test.ts`, then run lint.
